title: Conversation without an unspoken debt

captions.emotions: Feeling obliged to give something back

meaning: You can thoughtfully clarify an expectation of reciprocity without making a story you have heard into a debt to reveal just as much about yourselves.
text: Reciprocity in conversation does not always feel free. On your Vishuddha, the Hermit in the physical position helps you explain a pattern you noticed and share a considered account of it. The Devil in energy supports honesty about binding conversational conditions: recognising which answer seems owed for something already said. The Devil in emotions has a different role, experiencing attachment to receiving something in return. Wanting to clarify the condition and feeling that a response is obligatory are distinct.

For example, a personal account is followed by “I shared something, so now it is your turn”. You reflect on the phrase and explain that listening did not mean promising a personal disclosure. **A story you hear creates no unspoken debt**. You can want greater reciprocity and say so directly. Yet attentive sympathy may still feel insufficient if a matching admission was expected. That expectation becomes the subject of conversation rather than evidence that either of you is ungrateful.

The vulnerable point is trying to use explanation to cancel the feeling of obligation or the desire for equal openness immediately. Analysis then becomes another way to obtain the required answer. Constructive honesty helps distinguish a named expectation from an accepted commitment. You can acknowledge wanting a reciprocal account while allowing each other to choose its content and timing, without demanding repayment for something already heard.
